Alex: Heads-up — we saw a 12% P99 increase on hosted when large streaming responses hit the edge. profiling points at the host-side dechunker + gRPC HPACK decode hotpath.
Maya: Ugh. Any idea whether it's HPACK decode time or the buffer handling around it?
Alex: Both, but traces show long waits inside `dechunker.py` where we call into the grpc read loop. HPACK decode spikes when payloads have many headers (client metadata + routing).
Sam: Is this limited to HTTP/2/gRPC or seen on http1 as well?
Alex: Mostly gRPC. http1 path looks OK. Also noticed KV cache miss storms correlate with the same requests — possible interplay (reallocs causing more fragmentation).
Liu: Can you paste the flamegraph snippet?
Alex: Sure — here's the critical section from perf on a host worker: ```
  38.2%  runtime  dechunker::read_frame
  21.7%  grpc    hpack::decode
  12.4%  allocator  jemalloc:arena_run_alloc
  8.9%   kvcache  kv::lookup_miss
```
Maya: That `jemalloc:arena_run_alloc` hit is telling — frequent small allocs during streaming. We should try a pre-allocated slab or pooled buffers for dechunker.
Sam: Also check our kernel selection fallback: when requests are big we sometimes switch to the slow CPU-bound kernel for postprocessing which amplifies latency. Could be coincident.
Alex: Yep. I correlated traces: when HPACK time > 5ms, we sometimes fall back into `generic_decode_kernel` (slow path) for chunk reassembly.
Liu: Prioritization idea: 1) reduce alloc churn in dechunker (pool), 2) short-circuit HPACK for known safe clients (cache decoded headers), 3) fix fast-path kernel selection so it doesn't degrade under transient pressure.
Maya: For (2) can we add a small LRU keyed by connection id + header hash? 128 entries should cover most hot clients.
Sam: We need to be careful re memory and correctness — HPACK dynamic table interactions tricky. But a cached header vector for identical header sequences is OK.
Alex: I pushed a quick prototype branch `hot/dechunker-pool` with a pooled buffer allocator and recorded a local perf run: P99 down 6% and `jemalloc` ticks cut ~60%. Patch: ```
  // pseudo
  pool = BufferPool::with_capacity(256, 16k);
  let buf = pool.get_or_create();
  read_into(&mut buf);
```
Maya: Nice. Can you run it on a perf canary in staging? deploy-bot: `deploy staging hot/dechunker-pool` will schedule a canary.
DeployBot: deploy started for hot/dechunker-pool -> staging-cluster-3 (canary).
Alex: Canary numbers after 30m: steady-state P50 same, P95 -3%, P99 -7% on streaming RPCs. HPACK decode time unchanged but total wall time improved thanks to fewer alloc stalls.
Liu: Good win. Next: kernel pick. I instrumented the kernel-selector: when windowed CPU usage > 70% we downgrade to generic kernel because fast kernel has a memory pattern that briefly oversubscribes caches. We should make the selector consider recent allocation rate and KV cache pressure before switching.
Sam: Agree. Add two signals: `alloc_rate_next_1s` and `kv_miss_rate_5s` to the policy. If alloc_rate spikes but kv_miss low, prefer fast kernel.
Maya: Also, we saw grpc HPACK overhead is worst when header sets include `x-routing-*` lots. Can we truncate or normalize incoming routing headers earlier at the edge (before HPACK decode)? Maybe route metadata can live in a compressed binary proto header.
Alex: I'll prototype normalization middleware that strips/encodes repeating routing keys. Could drop into ingress sidecar.
Liu: On KV cache: I observed repeated small requests evicting hot KV entries (kvcache uses LFU-ish). Suggest bumping min-residence time for small keys and enabling prefetch on sequential token requests.
Sam: We should also add a regression test: synthetic stream with heavy header churn + small token requests to catch this in CI.
Maya: TL;DR action list: 1) land dechunker-pool canary if no regression (Alex) 2) prototype HPACK header-cache LRU (Maya) 3) change kernel selector signals and run canary (Liu+Sam) 4) ingress normalization spike (Alex) 5) CI synthetic test (Sam).
Alex: I'll kick off PRs and link them here. Also adding perf dashboards for `alloc_rate` and `kv_miss_rate`.
Sam: Thanks — if kernel selector fix is nontrivial prioritize a small config toggle to keep fast kernel pinned for the canary.
Maya: One more note: add a metric for `dechunker_buffer_reuse_rate` so we can see pool effectiveness.
Alex: Good call. Adding that now.
Liu: Nice thread. If anyone finds any regressions from the canary ping here. :thumbsup:
